flags.why: The word means “mất dạy” (ill-mannered or insolent), rather than praising someone's wit ([Wiktionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/lót_tích)).
This expression can insult someone as “mất dạy,” but its tags provide no insult warning ([Wiktionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/lót_tích)).
The example expresses extreme rudeness, with a vulgar intensifier, rather than cleverness ([Wiktionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/lót_tích)).
The word describes successive pointed shapes rising to uneven heights, rather than things being tangled ([Rung dictionary](https://v2.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/Lô_xô)).
flags.fix: rising in successive peaks at uneven heights

flags.why: The wires example uses the word to mean tangled, which is not its meaning ([Rung dictionary](https://v2.rung.vn/dict/vn_vn/Lô_xô)).
flags.fix: Những ngọn núi đá lô xô phía xa. = Rocky peaks rise at uneven heights in the distance.
